anomalies.observed: In the 'WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES' block, the 'Water Height Sensor' sub-circuit places PR1 ('LIDAR', footprint PB_1.25mm) together with its 5-pin header H4, and the connector's pins are drawn wired to the main, non-isolated I2C bus (I2C_SDA / I2C_SCL, plus +5V and GND). So the TF-Luna LiDAR shares the same bus as the EZO-RTD, the ADM3260 primary sides and the H5/H6 sensor headers.
anomalies.expected: The specification states that PR1 is documentation only and is not connected to anything: 'the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free - i.e. it is not connected to any net in this design,' and that 'The water-level sensing that is actually wired and actually used by firmware is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor read on two ESP32 GPIOs'.

evidence.quote: WATER LEVEL SENSOR/SWITCHES ... Water Height Sensor ... PR1 LIDAR ... H4 PB_1.25mm ... I2C_SDA ... I2C_SCL (sheet 1)
the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no, in_bom: yes, and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free - i.e. it is not connected to any net in this design.
The water-level sensing that is actually wired and actually used by firmware is an HC-SR04-style ultrasonic sensor read on two ESP32 GPIOs

anomalies.impact: The TF-Luna LiDAR would be present on the shared I2C bus (loading it and answering at its own I2C address), and the intended ultrasonic water-level interface is not provided by this build, so water-level sensing would behave differently from the specified design.

parsed.summary: The board largely matches the specification, but the TF-Luna LiDAR (PR1) that the specification explicitly says is not connected to any net is drawn wired onto the main non-isolated I2C bus via header H4, a connectivity deviation that would put the LiDAR on the shared I2C bus and replace the intended ultrasonic water-level interface.
